logline: A mom finds her son's money gone - he spent $2,000 (actually $3,000) on streetwear to resell - and gives him one week to make every dollar back; after days of no sales and a late-night doubt, the orders flood in, he ships around the clock, she ends up packing beside him, and he has already bought more stock.

hook.mechanic: Cold open mid-confrontation: title 'MOMMY SAID I'D FAIL' while mom storms through the door brandishing his empty wallet - 'Nate! Where is all your money?' - and slams it on the desk; a rapid-fire Q&A ('You had $2,000.' 'I spent it.' 'On what?' 'My business.') in one 4.5 s take, then a whip into the wide reveal of a room stacked with clothes.

montage.description: Two wordless locked-off montages. (1) 13.08-17.18, 11 shots, the grind: same frontal desk set-up, jump cuts and speed-ramped smears as Nate holds up a red spider-web hoodie, lays out hoodies, shoots them on his phone, works the laptop, packs and tapes a box, then stares at his phone - nothing. (2) 37.37-40.90, 8 shots, 'days passing': same desk, fast-motion packing while the light flips between warm day, cool day and blue night every 0.2-0.8 s. Keep the locked frame and the light-flip device; the speed-ramp ghosting does the work of a time-lapse.

beats.summary: HOOK: mom storms in with his wallet - 'Where is all your money?' 'I spent it.' 'On what?' 'My business.'
Reveal + challenge: wide of a room stacked with clothes; '$2,000 on clothes?' 'Actually, three.' -> 'Then prove it. One week. Make your $2,000 back.' Nose-to-nose: 'All of it?' 'Every dollar.'
MONTAGE 1: wordless grind at the desk - hoodies, photos, listings, packing - then a blank look at the phone.
Night doubt: laptop glow, 'I spent everything.' Mom in the doorway: 'You don't have to prove anything to me.' 'Yes, I do.' Messages come in - 'Wait.' 'Mom.'
Breakthrough: crash zoom to his face, sale notifications glowing in his eyes - 'Yo.' - star-jump 'Yeah!'
Night shipping time-lapse; stock piles up, mom appears in the doorway: 'What happened?' 'They're selling.' 'All of them?' 'I'm trying.'
MONTAGE 2: days pass in flickers of daylight and night while he packs.
Exhausted, he faceplants into a hoodie; mom joins him - 'What are you doing? You're doing it wrong.'
Payoff: packing side by side, high five - 'Told ya.' 'Don't get cocky.' Whip to a closet full of boxes: 'You bought more?' 'Maybe.' Snap zoom on mom's horrified face.
Real-life tag: CG Nate standing in the real room morphs into the creator; garage, waterfront dinner, balcony - 'respect.'

transcription: faster-whisper 'small' (CPU, int8) with word timestamps, cross-checked against the burned-in word-by-word captions. Whisper stretched three segments over music: 'I spent everything' (13.44-18.30, real 17.40-18.30), 'What are you doing?' (38.08-45.31, real 44.70-45.31) and 'You bought more?' (51.10-52.44, real 51.80-52.44) - caption timing used. Added from captions: 'Nate!' (0.30), 'Yeah!' (27.50), 'Huh.' (52.80).
why_it_works: The hook is a prop and a number: an empty wallet waved in the doorway and '$2,000' in the first 3 s - stakes are concrete and instantly readable.
Escalation by one word: 'Actually, three.' cut to mom's clenched-teeth close-up is the reel's biggest laugh and makes Nate a cheeky, likeable underdog.
A clean contract - 'One week. Make your $2,000 back.' 'Every dollar.' - sealed in a nose-to-nose profile ECU, so the viewer knows exactly what success looks like.
Wordless locked-off montages (same frame, jump cuts, speed-ramp ghosting, day/night light flips) show time and effort with zero dialogue and are cheap to generate as one set-up.
The emotional low is quiet: night, laptop glow, mom softening ('You don't have to prove anything to me') - the warm doorway light behind him is the visual for her support.
The turn is a visual gag, not a line: notification glow in his pupils and a star-jump 'Yeah!' - big cartoon acting at the peak.
Mom moves from antagonist to teammate (packing beside him, 'You're doing it wrong'), a more wholesome arc than revenge, widening the audience.
The button is a callback reversal: he already bought more stock, snap zoom on her horrified face - ends on a laugh, not a lecture.
The CG-to-real morph in the same room plus 'respect.' and 'Based on a true story' sell the creator as the character and feed the 'Comment SHEET' CTA.
undetermined: Music not identified; no true silence (auto draft found none).
'Yes.' at 7.86 speaker unclear (shot change, both on screen); given to Nate.
'Nate!' (0.30), 'Yeah!' (27.50) and 'Huh.' (52.80) are caption only; 'Huh.' speaker inferred (Nate, smirking).

Montage counts depend on how jump cuts are read: in shots 7-17 the smeared state changes are counted as cuts, the speed-ramped motion inside shot 15 is not; in shots 26-33 each light flip (day/night) is counted as a cut.
Shots 24 and 34 are long locked-off time-lapse takes with motion ghosting; further micro jumps inside them (auto detector fired 12 times in shot 24) are not counted.
Shot 37 (ECU mom) starts inside a snap-zoom smear; the cut point (53.30) is estimated - it may be a crash zoom with no cut.
Shot 38 is the CG character placed in a photoreal copy of the creator's room - counted as animated; the 3 white flash frames at 54.32-54.57 are the morph, folded into shot 39.
The file is a 60 fps container; about a quarter of frames are duplicates, so source frame rate is lower; short-shot durations accurate to about +/-0.03 s.
